---
title: "Project Result Contracts"
description: "Exact cleaning rules, calculations, filenames, and CSV fields used for automated project checks."
---

## Why the Contracts Are Fixed

The result files connect each report to executable code. They allow the
instructor to rerun approximately 20 submissions and identify discrepancies
without turning automated output into the whole grade.

Students generate these files from their MATLAB or R script. They must not type
or edit calculated values manually.

## Project 1 Calculation Rules

1. Keep rows with nonmissing `outdoor_temp_c` and `heating_energy_kwh` for all
   summaries and models.
2. Fit the linear and quadratic temperature models with `polyfit`.
3. Calculate RMSE using the supplied `model_rmse.m` function.
4. Define the sensitivity observation as the row with the largest absolute
   residual from the quadratic fit.
5. Remove only that row, refit the quadratic model, and repeat the assigned
   prediction.

The MATLAB code filenames use underscores because MATLAB identifiers cannot
contain hyphens:

```text
group_01_project1.m
model_rmse.m
```

The result file retains the Blackboard group identifier:

```text
group-01-project1-results.csv
```

Download the header-only
[Project 1 result schema](schemas/project-1-results-schema.csv).

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `group_id` | Assigned identifier such as `group-01` |
| `n_rows_raw`, `n_rows_usable` | Rows before and after removing incomplete response/temperature rows |
| `mean_outdoor_temp_c`, `mean_heating_energy_kwh` | Complete-case means |
| `linear_intercept`, `linear_temp_coefficient` | Linear fit coefficients in mathematical order |
| `linear_rmse_kwh`, `linear_r_squared` | Linear in-sample diagnostics |
| `quadratic_intercept`, `quadratic_temp_coefficient`, `quadratic_temp2_coefficient` | Quadratic fit coefficients in mathematical order |
| `quadratic_rmse_kwh`, `quadratic_r_squared` | Quadratic in-sample diagnostics |
| `assigned_prediction_temp_c`, `assigned_prediction_kwh` | Required interpolation input and quadratic prediction |
| `sensitivity_removed_observation_id`, `sensitivity_prediction_kwh` | Fixed sensitivity removal and repeated prediction |

## Project 2 Cleaning and Modeling Rules

1. Remove repeated `observation_id` values, keeping the first occurrence.
2. Remove rows incomplete in any of the seven supplied training variables.
3. Treat `day_type` as a category with `weekday` as the reference level.
4. Fit one frozen `lm` formula using `heating_energy_kwh` as the response.
5. Use only `outdoor_temp_c`, `occupancy_count`, `wind_speed_m_s`, `day_type`,
   approved transformations (`I`, `poly`, `log`, or `sqrt`), and defensible
   interactions.
6. Define the baseline as the mean cleaned training response.
7. Use RMSE and MAE on both the training and validation data.
8. For sensitivity, remove the training row with the largest absolute
   standardized residual, refit the same formula, and recalculate validation
   RMSE.

The model plan is frozen before the validation file is released. The formula
may differ by group, but the cleaning, metrics, and sensitivity procedure do
not.

The checker flags a model for human review when it improves validation RMSE by
less than 45% relative to the mean-response baseline. A flag is not an automatic
grade or misconduct decision; it identifies a result that needs inspection.

Download the header-only [Project 2 result
schema](schemas/project-2-results-schema.csv) and [validation-prediction
schema](schemas/project-2-validation-predictions-schema.csv).

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `group_id` | Assigned identifier |
| `n_training_rows_raw`, `n_training_rows_unique`, `n_training_rows_usable` | Fixed cleaning checkpoints |
| `n_validation_rows` | Number of released validation observations |
| `model_formula` | Frozen R formula converted to one line of text |
| `primary_coefficient_name`, `primary_coefficient_estimate` | One coefficient selected for interpretation, using its exact R name |
| `baseline_value_kwh`, `baseline_validation_rmse_kwh` | Mean-training-response baseline and its validation error |
| `training_rmse_kwh`, `training_mae_kwh`, `training_r_squared` | Training diagnostics |
| `validation_rmse_kwh`, `validation_mae_kwh` | Validation diagnostics |
| `sensitivity_removed_observation_id` | Largest standardized-residual training row |
| `sensitivity_validation_rmse_kwh` | Validation RMSE after the fixed sensitivity refit |

The prediction file contains exactly one row per validation
`observation_id`, in validation-file order, and one numeric `prediction_kwh`.

## What the Automated Checker Does Not Grade

Passing the file contract does not establish a good project. The instructor
still reviews figures, interpretation, modeling judgment, limitations,
communication, and the AI-use appendix in the PDF.
